item.processing_route: Vacuum-arc melting with high purity elements (purity > 99.9 wt.%) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere
item.test_conditions: Room temperature and high-temperature (600-1000 °C) mechanical properties, including Vickers hardness, compressive yield strength, and plastic strain
key_findings: The alloys exhibit a typical dendritic and eutectic structure
The Vickers hardness increases with increasing Ta and W contents, ranging from 546 HV0.2 to 1135 HV0.2

records.text: Paper card. Question: What are the microstructure, mechanical properties, and high-temperature stability of novel low-activation VCrFeTaxWx high-entropy alloys?. System: VCrFeTaxWx (x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 1) high-entropy alloys. Processing: Vacuum-arc melting with high purity elements (purity > 99.9 wt.%) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere. Test conditions: Room temperature and high-temperature (600-1000 °C) mechanical properties, including Vickers hardness, compressive yield strength, and plastic strain. Findings: The alloys exhibit a typical dendritic and eutectic structure; The Vickers hardness increases with increasing Ta and W contents, ranging from 546 HV0.2 to 1135 HV0.2; The compressive yield strengths of T0.1 and T0.2 alloys are 1341 MPa and 1742 MPa, with plastic strains of 42.2% and 35.7%, respectively; The alloys show excellent heat-softening resistance at 600-800 °C, with yield strengths exceeding 1000 MPa; The high-temperature mechanical properties are promising for applications in extreme environments, such as fusion reactors. Mechanism: The solid-solution strengthening and the formation of hard Laves phases precipitated in particles contribute to alloy strengthening. Future work: Further development of the current concepts to produce refractory high-temperature structural materials, which are candidate alloys for fusion reactors. Quote: "the alloy system of VCrFeTa0.1W0.1, VCrFeTa0.2W0.2, VCrFeTa0.3W0.3, VCrFeTa0.4W0.4, and VCrFeTaW fully met the VEC, δ-Ω, and δ-△Hmix criteria"
